text: Explorer 1 launched on January 31, 1958 (February 1 UTC) from Cape Canaveral as the first US satellite.
Its oval orbit had a perigee of about 358 km and an apogee of about 2,550 km, completing a lap every 114.8 minutes.
It carried a cosmic-ray detector built by James Van Allen of the University of Iowa.
At high altitudes the counter dropped to zero counts because it was overwhelmed by intense trapped radiation.
Explorer 1's data led to the discovery of Earth's trapped radiation belts, now known as the Van Allen belts.
Mercury batteries powered the main transmitter for 31 days and the low-power beacon for 105 days.
Last transmission May 23, 1958 per NASA Science (some pages say May 21).
safe_text: NASA Science records the last transmission on May 23, 1958 (some accounts cite May 21).

text: Explorer 1 orbited silently until re-entering Earth's atmosphere on March 31, 1970 after more than 58,000 orbits.
